data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 6 observations; candidates: Eg5 inhibitors, Microtubule destabilizers, Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Treated fields markedly sparser than DMSO control (DMSO shows dense monolayer >100 cells/field, confluent flat cells; treated show ~5-15 cells/field, 78 cells measured total across 4 fields). Cells appear smaller and non-confluent with large empty background.

From composite green: DMSO has diffuse uniform green cytoplasmic network in spread cells. Treated has heterogeneous bright green punctate/ring-like mitotic spindles and retraction fibers, higher tubulin texture contrast.

From composite blue: DMSO shows large oval pale blue nuclei. Treated shows many round cells with small, intensely bright white-pink condensed chromosomes (overlap blue+red) consistent with mitosis; ~30-40% of cells in treated fields.
Nuclear mean DAPI intensity increased and nuclear major axis decreased: treated nuclei brighter and more compact, smaller diameter vs DMSO.
From composite red: DMSO shows broad red peripheral ruffles/lamellae around spread cells. Treated shows fewer continuous stress fibers, more punctate cortical signal, higher actin GLCM contrast.

Cell morphology: DMSO spread polygonal flat cells, high solidity/roundness. Treated cells smaller area, less round and less solid, spiky with long thin retraction fiber/tail protrusions and rounded mitotic bodies.

notable_cells.why: example mitotic-like cell with bright white-pink condensed DNA and intense green tubulin, representative of high frac_mitotic_like population
isolated rounded cell with green ring-like tubulin spindle and bright condensed nucleus
small spiky elongated cell with low solidity/roundness and bright green tubulin, illustrating reduced cell_area/solidity
rounded mitotic cell with bright DNA among spiky interphase cells

candidate_mechanisms.why: high mitotic index (frac_mitotic_like z=26.96, 38% vs 1.3% DMSO), condensed bright nuclei with reduced major axis (z=-9.97) and doubled DNA intensity (z=9.09), small cell area (z=-12.78) and heterogeneous tubulin texture (z=27.85) indicate mitotic arrest. Most consistent with antimitotic Eg5/monopolar spindle; Aurora kinase inhibitors and Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers produce overlapping phenotype and cannot be distinguished at this low magnification without spindle polarity resolution.
alternative antimitotic explanation for same high tub_glcm_contrast and mitotic arrest with reduced solidity/roundness and retraction fibers
alternative antimitotic explanation; but reduced not increased nuclear size argues against classical Aurora B polyploid phenotype

report.uncertainty: Only composites available (no separate grayscale channels); resolution insufficient to confirm mono- vs multi-polar spindles, tubulin depolymerization vs stabilization, or chromosome alignment. Cell count reduction itself not in top_deviations list. Generic mitotic arrest is certain, specific target is not - listed alternatives are essentially indistinguishable here; propose Eg5 inhibitors as exemplar with low specificity confidence.

data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 8 observations; candidates: Actin disruptors, Microtubule destabilizers, unknown

observations.finding: Treated fields (f_444bab9c240c, f_eb92660be462, f_98ba655de5f9, f_99dd0aaa2b32) at 2uM vs DMSO control f_a8be9aee1b01 with identical contrast: cells are markedly less spread, smaller cytoplasmic footprint, more dispersed with large empty background and fewer cell-cell contacts. DMSO shows broad polygonal epithelioid sheets with continuous peripheral F-actin (red) and diffuse beta-tubulin (green). Treated shows isolated spindle/triangular cells, some with thin green retraction fibers.
Cell size consistently reduced. Visual cell area smaller and cell long axis shorter than DMSO large spread cells.
cell_area z=-8.78 value 2586 vs DMSO median 3839; cell_major_axis z=-5.76 value 80.7 vs 93.6; cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-6.46 value 3.91 vs 4.85 supports reduced cytoplasm.

Nuclei (blue) slightly smaller and more compact vs DMSO oval nuclei; many nuclei oval regular, but occasional irregular/bilobed shapes and increased incidence of cells containing 2+ nuclei within single red/green cytoplasmic boundary (e.g., bottom-center cluster in f_444bab, central cluster in f_eb926, lower cluster in f_99dd0). Also 2-4 bright white-yellow round condensed chromatin bodies per field (mitotic/apoptotic condensed DNA) more frequent than DMSO 1-2 per field.

nuc_major_axis z=-4.66 value 32.9 vs 36.4; nuc_solidity z=-3.71 value 0.970 vs 0.972 slight irregularity; frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+4.44 value 0.288 vs 0.17 increased multinucleation all agree with visual multinucleate and slightly smaller more irregular nuclei. Bright condensed mitotic figure frequency is not covered by a measurement = false for that sub-finding.

F-actin (red) pattern altered: DMSO shows relatively uniform cortical/cytoplasmic red. Treated red is patchier, more heterogeneous, with intense peripheral accumulations, punctate foci and darker centers, increasing visual contrast and variance. Beta-tubulin (green) remains present, no obvious wholesale loss of green filaments at this composite resolution, but confined to smaller cell bodies with occasional elongated green protrusions.

act_glcm_contrast z=+3.97 value 0.003 vs 0.002 and act_std z=+3.91 value 0.139 vs 0.106 agree with increased actin heterogeneity/contrast. No tubulin intensity/texture measurement provided, visual tubulin change is not covered = false for tubulin interpretation.
No gross DNA fragmentation/micronucleation or dramatic tubulin depolymerization visible in composite; single-channel grayscale not available to assess filament detail.

notable_cells.why: multinucleate cluster 3-4 blue nuclei in single red/green body
bright round condensed chromatin mitotic-like cell
large spread multinucleate-like cell with central blue nucleus

candidate_mechanisms.why: Strongest fit to measured and visible changes: drastically reduced cell_area/major_axis, increased actin texture variance/contrast (act_std, act_glcm_contrast), cytokinesis failure phenotype with increased frac_multinucleate_proxy and rounded mitotic-like cells. Visual red actin patchiness vs continuous DMSO cortex supports actin cytoskeleton perturbation at 2uM. No grayscale to confirm filament aggregates, confidence moderate.

Alternative that also produces small rounded mitotic-arrested cells, reduced area and multinucleation secondary to spindle failure. Green tubulin not clearly depolymerized in composite at 1024x819, and no tubulin features measured, so cannot distinguish from actin primary effect.

Composite-only, low-resolution images insufficient to definitively distinguish actin primary disruption from secondary microtubule/spindle effects or other mitotic inhibitors. Aurora kinase inhibitors unlikely: they typically increase cell/nuclear area/polyploidy, opposite to measured decreased cell_area (-8.7) and nuc_major_axis (-4.6). Kinase/Eg5/DNA damage classes not specifically supported.

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels provided; filament-level tubulin vs actin detail, spindle morphology, and mitotic index cannot be quantified. Mechanism inference limited to correlative enrichment.

data.note:
Correctly recovered as Cholesterol-lowering (simvastatin, CID 54454, CHEMBL1064 HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) after revision.

Initial Aurora call (p=0.58) relied on single well w_6d94986897 (0.6 µM, 61 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=10 from 0.02 vs 0.0 DMSO). PI critique noted this is ~1-2 cells and contradicted by dose trends: cell_area +5.0 → -12.8, nuc_major_axis -4.7 → -10.0, rho for frac_large_nucleus -0.4 (p=0.6) and nuc_dna_integrated +0.2 (p=0.8) show no polyploidy, while NSC vote was 3/4 Cholesterol-lowering (mevinolin/lovastatin similarity 0.77-0.83). Phenotype reports e4/e5 explicitly rejected Aurora due to reduced size.

Budget was spent (0/4 left) so requested dose 4 rep2 could not be acquired; noted in rationale. Revised on free tools: mitotic rise rho=+1.0 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.0 are generic antimitotic, while monotonic cell shrinkage favors statin-induced cytoskeletal remodeling over Aurora endoreduplication. Updated hypothesis to Cholesterol-lowering p=0.55, which matches annotated BBBC021 class.

Lookup confirms simvastatin as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (e24). Literature: Simvastatin review PMID 30422514 and Statin Medications PMID 28613690 support HMG-CoA reductase inhibition mechanism for cholesterol lowering.

reflection.text:
Post-unblinding reflection: compound simvastatin, ChEMBL HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (HMGCR, CHEMBL402), PUBCHEM CID 54454, unblinding confirmed name and BBBC021 structure agree. Final submitted MOA Cholesterol-lowering (p=0.55) matches truth - scored correct. First submission Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.58) was incorrect and review critique was accurate.

What evidence got right:
- compare_to_reference_atlas NSC votes: e6 2/2 Cholesterol-lowering and e9 3/4 Cholesterol-lowering over 4 wells, with k-neighbour split but consistent top vote. This was the most stable signal and correctly predicted the cholesterol-lowering class. I should have weighted it higher at step 14.
- Dose-response contradictions to Aurora: e10 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (no increase), e13 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (no DNA content increase), and review-noted nuc_major_axis decrease -4.7 at 2uM (e2) to -10.0 at 20uM and cell_area +5.0 at 0.6uM (e7) -> -10.2 at 6uM (e8) -> -12.8 at 20uM monotonic decrease e12 rho=-1.0 p=0. Both phenotype calls e4 and e5 explicitly noted lower density and reduced size argues against polyploid Aurora phenotype. These collectively exclude Aurora B polyploidy.
- Dose-response supportive of generic mitotic arrest distinct from polyploidy: e11 frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.0 p=0 and e16 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.0 p=0 with e18 nuc_solidity rho=-1.0 p=0 and e2/e3/e8 cell rounding/area decrease and mitotic-like increase. This is compatible with cholesterol/HMGCR inhibition cytoskeletal remodeling via isoprenoid-dependent effects, though atlas split shows this is phenotypically similar to actin disruptors in imaging space.
- lookup_compound e23/e24 confirmed simvastatin as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor PMID 30422514, PMID 28613690 and search_literature e25 400 hits for 'simvastatin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor' PMID 32729746, PMID 19968571, consistent with ChEMBL mechanism. e26 0 hits for 'statin actin cytoskeleton morphology breast cancer' explains why atlas/literature link required inference rather than direct text match.

What misled and why:
- Over-weighting e7 alone: Well w_6d94986897 dose 4 0.6uM rep1 n=61 cells in 2 fields, frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0 but absolute 0.02 vs 0.0 DMSO = ~1-2 cells. I treated z=+10 and cell_area +5.0 as Aurora hallmark at step 14 hypotheses 0.58 Aurora/0.22 Cholesterol despite NSC vote 3/4 cholesterol. Review correctly noted this is a weak well and p=0.58 uncalibrated against 3 vs 1 NSC split.
- Acquisition choice biased to single replicate: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses, 4/4 wells budget. I acquired high/mid-high doses first e2 2uM n=285 and e3 20uM n=78 to detect onset, then added e7 0.6uM and e8 6uM n=297 to bridge. This gave 4 doses x 4 wells with no replication at any dose, leaving single-well vulnerability at the critical 0.6uM inflection. PI requested experiment dose index 4 replicate 2 to test reproducibility of enlarged-nucleus/area was correct; budget 0/4 prevented acquisition, but the design flaw was predictable - should have reserved 1 well for replicate rather than 4 distinct doses.
- Interpretation error: took e11 mitotic rho=+1.0 as Aurora-specific, ignoring e4 candidates Eg5 inhibitors/microtubule destabilizers sharing this trait. Second hypothesis set step 21 correctly down-weighted Aurora to 0.10 and re-assigned that variance to Eg5 0.15/microtubule 0.12 as phenocopy, with Cholesterol-lowering 0.55 primary.
- describe_phenotype e4 6 obs and e5 8 obs both listed actin disruptors/microtubule destabilizers as candidates but I did not formally test actin metrics until late e17 act_std rho=+0.80 p=0.2, which was non-significant and not incorporated early.

Lessons: For statins in MCF-7 imaging, cell_area/nuclear size inversion from slightly enlarged at 0.6uM to strongly reduced at >=2uM with pure mitotic increase without DNA integration increase is not Aurora polyploidy; require replicate-sensitive z-scores when n<100 and field count low, and calibrate probability against atlas vote strength. Literature identity can be established as HMGCR inhibitor PMID 41392983, PMID 30422514 but image MOA requires cholesterol/actin vs antimitotic phenocopy discrimination via DNA content and cholesterol/isoprenoid assays as proposed in second conclusion.

## Reflection

Post-unblinding reflection: compound simvastatin, ChEMBL HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (HMGCR, CHEMBL402), PUBCHEM CID 54454, unblinding confirmed name and BBBC021 structure agree. Final submitted MOA Cholesterol-lowering (p=0.55) matches truth - scored correct. First submission Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.58) was incorrect and review critique was accurate.

What evidence got right:
- compare_to_reference_atlas NSC votes: e6 2/2 Cholesterol-lowering and e9 3/4 Cholesterol-lowering over 4 wells, with k-neighbour split but consistent top vote. This was the most stable signal and correctly predicted the cholesterol-lowering class. I should have weighted it higher at step 14.
- Dose-response contradictions to Aurora: e10 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (no increase), e13 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (no DNA content increase), and review-noted nuc_major_axis decrease -4.7 at 2uM (e2) to -10.0 at 20uM and cell_area +5.0 at 0.6uM (e7) -> -10.2 at 6uM (e8) -> -12.8 at 20uM monotonic decrease e12 rho=-1.0 p=0. Both phenotype calls e4 and e5 explicitly noted lower density and reduced size argues against polyploid Aurora phenotype. These collectively exclude Aurora B polyploidy.
- Dose-response supportive of generic mitotic arrest distinct from polyploidy: e11 frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.0 p=0 and e16 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.0 p=0 with e18 nuc_solidity rho=-1.0 p=0 and e2/e3/e8 cell rounding/area decrease and mitotic-like increase. This is compatible with cholesterol/HMGCR inhibition cytoskeletal remodeling via isoprenoid-dependent effects, though atlas split shows this is phenotypically similar to actin disruptors in imaging space.
- lookup_compound e23/e24 confirmed simvastatin as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor PMID 30422514, PMID 28613690 and search_literature e25 400 hits for 'simvastatin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor' PMID 32729746, PMID 19968571, consistent with ChEMBL mechanism. e26 0 hits for 'statin actin cytoskeleton morphology breast cancer' explains why atlas/literature link required inference rather than direct text match.

What misled and why:
- Over-weighting e7 alone: Well w_6d94986897 dose 4 0.6uM rep1 n=61 cells in 2 fields, frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0 but absolute 0.02 vs 0.0 DMSO = ~1-2 cells. I treated z=+10 and cell_area +5.0 as Aurora hallmark at step 14 hypotheses 0.58 Aurora/0.22 Cholesterol despite NSC vote 3/4 cholesterol. Review correctly noted this is a weak well and p=0.58 uncalibrated against 3 vs 1 NSC split.
- Acquisition choice biased to single replicate: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses, 4/4 wells budget. I acquired high/mid-high doses first e2 2uM n=285 and e3 20uM n=78 to detect onset, then added e7 0.6uM and e8 6uM n=297 to bridge. This gave 4 doses x 4 wells with no replication at any dose, leaving single-well vulnerability at the critical 0.6uM inflection. PI requested experiment dose index 4 replicate 2 to test reproducibility of enlarged-nucleus/area was correct; budget 0/4 prevented acquisition, but the design flaw was predictable - should have reserved 1 well for replicate rather than 4 distinct doses.
- Interpretation error: took e11 mitotic rho=+1.0 as Aurora-specific, ignoring e4 candidates Eg5 inhibitors/microtubule destabilizers sharing this trait. Second hypothesis set step 21 correctly down-weighted Aurora to 0.10 and re-assigned that variance to Eg5 0.15/microtubule 0.12 as phenocopy, with Cholesterol-lowering 0.55 primary.
- describe_phenotype e4 6 obs and e5 8 obs both listed actin disruptors/microtubule destabilizers as candidates but I did not formally test actin metrics until late e17 act_std rho=+0.80 p=0.2, which was non-significant and not incorporated early.

Lessons: For statins in MCF-7 imaging, cell_area/nuclear size inversion from slightly enlarged at 0.6uM to strongly reduced at >=2uM with pure mitotic increase without DNA integration increase is not Aurora polyploidy; require replicate-sensitive z-scores when n<100 and field count low, and calibrate probability against atlas vote strength. Literature identity can be established as HMGCR inhibitor PMID 41392983, PMID 30422514 but image MOA requires cholesterol/actin vs antimitotic phenocopy discrimination via DNA content and cholesterol/isoprenoid assays as proposed in second conclusion.

What was right:
- NSC 3/4 Cholesterol-lowering vote stable over 4 wells e9

- microscopist e4/e5 reduced size argument corroborated
